items.title: 7.2.2 Measuring the rate of a chemical reaction

source_refs.note: Topic 7.2.2, printed pages 147-148 (Figure 7.2 and Table 7.1), with Quick Check 7.3 as the self-check.

blocks.text: Measuring the rate of a reaction means determining the concentration of a reactant or product at regular intervals as the reaction progresses. A graph of concentration (y-axis) against time (x-axis) gives a curve. For the decomposition of HI to H2 and I2 at 500 degrees C the data of Table 7.1 give a falling curve, since HI is a reactant. The steepness of the curve reflects the progress of the reaction: the greater the slope near the start, the greater the rate. To measure the rate at, say, 100 seconds, draw a tangent to the curve there and measure its slope: complete a right-angled triangle with the tangent as hypotenuse; Figure 7.2 shows that in 100 sec the change in concentration is 0.04 mol dm-3, so rate = 0.04 / 100 = 4 x 10^-4 mol dm-3 s-1. This value means that the concentration of HI is decreasing by 2.5 moles per dm-3 every second during the given interval. A graph of the concentration of a product, H2 or I2, gives a rising curve whose tangent at 100 s gives the same value of rate, 4 x 10^-4 mol dm-3 s-1.
book_errors: same value of rate, 4 x 10^-4 mol dm-3 s-1

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: In Figure 7.2 the tangent falls by 0.04 mol dm-3 over about 160 s (the base CB of the triangle), not 100 s, so the rate at 100 s is 0.04 / 160 = about 2.5 x 10^-4 mol dm-3 s-1 (Table 7.1 gives a similar 2.6 x 10^-4 around 100 s). The HI concentration is falling by about 2.5 x 10^-4 mol dm-3, not 2.5 moles per dm3, every second.

blocks.alt: Grid graph of [HI] (0 to 0.10 mol dm-3) against Time (s) (0 to 350). A green falling curve passes through yellow data points at 50 to 350 s, from 0.10 at the start. A blue tangent touches the curve at 100 s and runs from 0.08 at the y-axis to below 0.04. A right-angled triangle ABC: vertical leg from A at 0.08 down to C at 0.04 on the y-axis, labelled 0.04 mol dm-3, and horizontal leg from C to B on the tangent at about 164 s.

blocks.text: The printed Figure 7.2 labels the y-axis '[H1]' and puts the letter X on the vertical axis and Y on the horizontal one; the axis is [HI], with Y vertical and X horizontal, as drawn above.
